title: The grain fleet
terrain: three lashed decks; open water at every edge; no terrain to hide behind
design_note: VOYAGE not battle: the fleet is under way and the objective is landfall. Privateers board from the map edges. GRAPPLE LINES ARE THE DENS -- each is a capturable structure that stops producing when cut, so boarding is an objective, not an ambush. Fliers dominant, riding impossible, armor sinks if it goes over the side. The Assembly could not build this fleet, so it bought one; the privateers were paid for in Anbar.
approaches: the weather deck|below, through the hold|the rigging (flying only)

title: Ur-Nashet, the last night
terrain: hanging gardens in rain: stepped terraces (+1 cost when wet), irrigation channels, one aqueduct span
design_note: PROLOGUE. Breaks the map laws on purpose -- a flashback is a memory, and memories are unreliable in the direction of making you look stronger than you were. No permadeath, no dens, no requisition, no forge, one weapon each, no repair. The garrison is fatigued and not a threat. The living patron stands over the temple terrace, never moves, never attacks, has no health bar, and watches. It goes still only AFTER the image is rubble and the scribe writes -- you cannot write down a god that people can still see.
approaches: the terraces (foot)|the aqueduct span (one tile)|the channels (flying only)

title: The North Wind Winds
terrain: a drowned valley: farmland on the exposed old shoreline, a residual lake at the rift's low point with a bell tower's submerged tip still visible, villages worked the dry ground seasonally
design_note: REGROUNDED AGAIN (2026-09-24): the 2026-09-23 pass rebuilt this terrain from rgn_stepped_coast's terrace scar text, which turned out to be the wrong region -- see chapters.ch_p_macuil's own corrected note. Terrain rebuilt a second time from rgn_drowned_march's actual scar ('a rift valley that filled; a lake with a visible former shoreline') and texture ('in dry years the top of a bell tower breaks the surface; villages sit on the new shoreline and farm the old one'): mostly open farmland (the exposed old shoreline, dry-year conditions) around a residual lake patch with the bell tower's tip as a landmark -- reusing ter_wall_face ('x') for the tip purely for its existing cost profile (impassable to ground, flying passes over), not for its 'wall/temple' name. objective_verb stays a placeholder default (seize) -- nothing in npcs.npc_macuil or the region's own row states an objective, only atmosphere and a doctrine match -- but this pass actually places a '*' seize tile in the grid, which the prior version never did (seize_pos would have resolved to map_grid.gd's not-found sentinel, making the old map's stated objective unreachable regardless of play). Seize tile sits on dry ground at the hermit's spot on the new shoreline, not in the water, so it's reachable on foot.
approaches: the shoreline farmland (foot)|the lake (flying only, ground blocked around the tower)

title: His Lake
terrain: the hermit's lake: his island on the north shore, Pelagos (the fisher commune) on the south, open water between that only the Isles' own pilots cross safely -- except one known shallow ford
design_note: Regrounded (2026-09-23) once locations.loc_hermit_lake/polities.pol_isles/settlements.set_pelagos were found (see ch_p_indech's own note for the correction and full connection). objective_verb='defend' was already set but turn_limit was 0, which silently made the defend-win condition (map_grid.gd's _check_defend_win, limit>0 required) unreachable -- set to 8, matching map_a02/map_v22/map_m22's precedent for the same objective_verb. Terrain rebuilt around a real chokepoint: pol_isles.comparative_advantage ('pilotage -- the Isles' crews are why anyone crosses safely') implies the open water isn't safely crossable without a local pilot, so a raiding ea_warlord reaching Pelagos needs a ford -- that ford, not the lake itself, is what's actually being defended. ea_warlord's movement_type is infantry (enemy_archetypes), so it can use the foot-only ford exactly like the player's own ground units; the old placeholder terrain had no ford at all, which would have made either side unable to reach the other.
approaches: the shores (foot)|the ford, 3 tiles wide (foot only)|open water (flying only)

title: The Lowest Terrace
terrain: the lowest of the Stepped Coast's three raised marine terraces, at the waterline, with the higher terraces rising behind it and the open sea beyond
design_note: New (2026-09-24). Grounded in locations.loc_lowest_terrace ('the Shadhavar; the song pulls the nearest enemy one tile a turn') and regions.rgn_stepped_coast's own scar ('three raised marine terraces, each a former shoreline, each with a ruined harbor at the wrong altitude') -- this is specifically the LOWEST of those three terraces, the one nearest the water, distinct from ch_p_indech's own site in the same region (a lake further out among the isles). Terrain: the upper terraces sit as a riding-blocked backdrop band, the lowest terrace itself is the open battlefield, the sea is the boundary beyond it. objective_verb='seize' is a placeholder default, same as every other paralogue map -- nothing in named.nmd_shadhavar or locations.loc_lowest_terrace states a win condition, only atmosphere. ea_shadhavar (enemy_archetypes) stands in for the creature itself, same pattern as ea_warlord standing in for Macuil and Indech's own capstone encounters -- the real pact/three-way-capture system and the song's always-on pull effect are NOT modeled in map_grid.gd, see this chapter's own note for the full scope flag.
approaches: the lowest terrace (foot, riding)|the upper terraces (riding blocked)|the sea (flying only)

title: The Mountain Above the Lake
terrain: a mountain rising above rgn_drowned_march's drowned lake, slopes ringing a nest plateau, the lake visible far below
design_note: New (2026-09-24). Grounded in locations.loc_simurgh_nest ('The mountain above the lake') and regions.rgn_drowned_march's own scar/texture -- the same lake ch_p_macuil's regrounded terrain sits beside, seen this time from the mountain above it rather than the drowned shoreline itself. Terrain: mountain slopes (riding blocked) ringing an open plateau where the nest sits, with the lake visible far below as a flying-only boundary. objective_verb='seize' is a placeholder default, same as every other paralogue map -- nothing in named.nmd_simurgh or locations.loc_simurgh_nest states a win condition. ea_simurgh (enemy_archetypes) stands in for the creature as a fightable capstone, same pattern as ea_warlord/ea_shadhavar -- but flagged more strongly here than elsewhere: named.nmd_simurgh reads as protective and benevolent ('foster-mother', 'cleanses corruption'), not adversarial, so treating her as a hostile boss spawn is a bigger simplification than for the Shadhavar or Macuil's own capstone fight. The real pact/feather system and her 5 HP/turn aura are NOT modeled in map_grid.gd.
approaches: the nest plateau (foot, riding)|the slopes (riding blocked)|the lake far below (flying only)

title: The Dove Colony
terrain: the Ashland's volcanic ash field, miasma throughout, ringing a clear central clearing -- the dove colony the Karkadann guards
design_note: New (2026-09-24). Grounded in locations.loc_dove_colony and regions.rgn_ashland's own scar/texture ('a volcanic field; spectacular soil, bad air' / 'miasma tiles live here and stop being generic fog'). Terrain reuses ter_miasma ('m', hazard_dmg=2, all movement types affected including flying, per its own existing cost row) for the ash field blanketing the region, with a clear central clearing (the dove colony itself, safe ground) players must cross the hazard to reach, and a clean foothold at the deploy edge so the encounter doesn't start with damage already ticking. objective_verb='seize' is a placeholder default, same as every other paralogue map. ea_karkadann (enemy_archetypes) stands in for the creature as a fightable capstone, same pattern as the other three Named stand-ins this session -- its real charge mechanic (bonus vs mounted units, stuck one turn after) is NOT modeled in map_grid.gd, which has no type-effectiveness or stun-after-attack system.
approaches: the clearing (foot, riding, safe)|the ash field (all movement, 2 HP/turn hazard)

title: The Interior of the Flats
terrain: the Glass Flats' interior: fused, straight-edged, featureless ground under a white sky -- open sightlines in every direction, nothing to break them
design_note: New (2026-09-24). Grounded in locations.loc_flats_interior and regions.rgn_glass_flats's own scar/texture ('fused ground, straight-edged, unmistakably made; nothing grows' / 'white sky, hard noon light, mineral color, a single figure legible at distance. Beautiful, not gothic'). Terrain deliberately reuses only ter_court ('.', plain cost-1 ground) throughout -- no new symbol, no hazard, on purpose: 'nothing grows' and 'a single figure legible at distance' both describe a stark, empty, sightline-open flat, the first paralogue map this session without any terrain variation at all. That emptiness is the grounded choice, not a placeholder shortcut. objective_verb='seize' stays the same reviewed placeholder as every paralogue map (see chapters.ch_p_anzu's own note for why sect_road's real 'purchase' precedent was considered and rejected here). ea_anzu (enemy_archetypes) stands in for the creature as a fightable capstone -- its real weapon-degrading touch and the literacy-contract system are NOT modeled in map_grid.gd.
approaches: the open flat (all movement, no cover, no chokepoints)

title: The Open Road
terrain: an open stretch of the Throat road, no landmark, no scar -- the road itself is the only feature, the Huma drifting somewhere overhead
design_note: New (2026-09-24). Grounded in locations.loc_open_road ('no fixed site') and regions.rgn_the_throat's own scar ('none; the road itself is the feature'). Terrain is a plain east-west road corridor, no hazard, no landmark -- deliberately featureless like ch_p_anzu's Flats, but shaped as a strip to cross rather than an open field, since 'the road itself is the feature'. objective_verb='escape' (not the usual paralogue placeholder 'seize') is the one real objective departure this session: nothing here is a fixed point to seize, and named.nmd_huma's own region row is explicit there is no site. Reuses map_grid.gd's existing escape/escort logic (min_solution_units units must reach the 'E' tile at the road's far end) -- same mechanism as map_a03, no new engine work. No boss spawn: named.nmd_huma is explicitly 'MAP HAZARD, NOT A MOUNT' with a stated kill-taboo, so unlike every other Named paralogue this session it is NOT represented as a fightable enemy -- see chapters.ch_p_huma's own note for the full reasoning. The two mook spawns (ea_looter, already grounded for 'opportunists working the toll road' on map_r16) are the actual combat; the Huma itself only appears in this text and the scene, drifting overhead, never targetable.
approaches: the road (all movement, open, no cover)
